songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy early set with standout Midnight Hour and Dancin' In The Street
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a tight blues‑rock set featuring Pigpen’s organ‑driven “In The Midnight Hour” and an explosive “Dancin’ In The Street” jam. Jerry’s lead work is hot and smoky throughout, while Bob and Phil provide solid rhythm and bass support. Highlights include “I Know You Rider,” “Good Morning Little School Girl,” and “Lindy.”
ai_show_review.review: September 16, 1966 at the Avalon Ballroom finds the early Dead firing on all cylinders. From the opening “I Know You Rider” through a gritty “It Hurts Me Too,” the band moves with a crisp, blues‑rock groove that feels both rehearsed and spontaneous. Pigpen’s organ takes center stage on “In The Midnight Hour,” turning the encore into a rousing showcase of his swampy voice and swirling keys. The centerpiece of the night is an electrifying “Dancin’ In The Street” jam where Jerry tears into smoky, jazz‑inflected leads that lock tightly with Phil’s steady torch‑like bass. Bob’s rhythm guitar and vocals sit forward in the mix, sounding unusually confident for a ’66 performance, while Bill keeps a tight, dynamic pulse despite the occasional thinness in the recorded drum mix. The set rounds out with bright renditions of “Good Morning Little School Girl,” “Lindy,” and a plaintive take on “It’s All Over Now Baby Blue,” making this Avalon show one of the most vibrant snapshots of the band’s formative era.

best_recording.reason: Soundboard source with mostly clear audio; captures Pigpen‑driven Midnight Hour and the fiery Dancin' In The Street jam with only slight buzz/clip.

band_performance.Jerry: Hot, smoky leads dominate the night—especially on “Dancin’ In The Street” and “In The Midnight Hour”—with jazz‑inflected runs and high‑speed bluegrass phrasing.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a solid, torch‑like bass foundation that underpins the band’s high‑energy grooves throughout the set.
band_performance.Bob: Vocals and rhythm guitar stand out as unusually confident for 1966, adding drive to “Good Morning Little School Girl,” “Lindy,” and other numbers.
band_performance.Billy: Drummers keep a tight, dynamic pulse; despite occasional thinness in the mix, their interplay with Jerry fuels the jam sections.
